title: Gangu Shah’s Service at the Baoli, Rise as a Hundiwal, and Request for Power

blocks.text: Guru Amar Das gives Gangu Shah useful service in the digging of the baoli, teaching him that livelihood should remain tied to labor and devotion rather than to self-display. From there his circumstances improve dramatically, and he is later asked to be blessed with the status of a Hundiwal financier.

Success, however, begins to loosen humility. After wealth and credit come, he mishandles trust and even refuses the Guru's own consignment, revealing how quickly worldly ascent can distort spiritual obligation.

Yet the story does not end there. Restored to service, he is sent toward the hills for butter-oil offerings, and the page prepares the reader for his increasingly dangerous desire to command reverence through power.
